name: Bar
title: Bar, Montenegro Ship Thickness Measurement and UTM
description: Ultrasonic thickness measurement in Bar, Montenegro and the Bay of Kotor: bulk carrier and ferry hull gauging, pre-purchase and renewal survey support.
h1: Ship Thickness Measurement in Bar and the Bay of Kotor, Montenegro
intro: Bar is Montenegro's main cargo port and the sea end of the railway to Belgrade, while the Bay of Kotor, a short drive north, combines a busy cruise call with a ship-repair tradition now focused on large yachts. Bulk carriers, general cargo ships, ferries to Italy and cruise ships make up most of the traffic. Atlantis NDT mobilises technicians from India to gauge them at berth, at anchor or in refit.

highlights.h: Bulk cargo on the Belgrade rail link
highlights.p: Bar's rail connection to Podgorica and Belgrade brings bulk carriers and general cargo ships serving Montenegro and Serbia, whose holds, hatch covers and ballast tanks can be gauged during or after their cargo calls.

Montenegro's full membership of the Paris MoU means foreign ships in Bar and Kotor face the same port state control regime as ships in Italian and Croatian ports, which raises the value of gauging before the call.

highlights.h: Yacht refit in the Bay of Kotor
highlights.p: The former commercial ship-repair site at Bijela has been redeveloped for large-yacht refit, and with the Tivat marina it brings steel-hulled yachts whose plating and tanks are gauged while they are out of the water.

port.h: The port of Bar and the Bay of Kotor
p: The port of Bar sits on Montenegro's southern coast and is the country's principal gateway for bulk and general cargo. It is linked by rail to Podgorica and on to Belgrade, which gives it a hinterland in Serbia as well as Montenegro, and its terminals handle dry bulk, general cargo, containers, ro-ro traffic and fuel imports. Ferries cross the Adriatic to Bari in Italy, carrying passengers, cars and trucks, with traffic peaking in summer. Ships waiting to berth lie at anchor off the port, on a more open stretch of coast than the sheltered bays further north.

Inspection demand in Bar comes mainly from bulk carriers and general cargo ships on working calls, many of them mid-size ships in regional trades, and from the ferries on the Bari route. For the cargo ships a gauging record matters at every sale, charter and renewal survey; the ferries carry the usual ro-pax concerns of vehicle decks, ramps and ballast tanks. Because there is no large commercial ship-repair yard at Bar itself, UTM in Montenegro is done alongside or at anchor, either to close out survey items or to prepare an estimate for a docking elsewhere in the Adriatic.

The Bay of Kotor adds a different side of Montenegrin shipping. Kotor is one of the Adriatic's best-known cruise calls, with ships berthing at the town or anchoring in the inner bay and tendering passengers ashore. Tivat, on the same bay, has grown around Porto Montenegro, a superyacht marina built on a former naval shipyard, and the site of the old commercial ship-repair yard at Bijela has been redeveloped for large-yacht refit. The bay has a long seafaring tradition: the University of Montenegro's Faculty of Maritime Studies is in Kotor, and Montenegrin officers and engineers serve widely in international fleets. Bar and the bay are close enough by road to be covered in a single mobilisation.

facilities.h: Where thickness gauging happens in Bar and the Bay of Kotor
p: In Bar, gauging is done on ships alongside at the cargo and ferry terminals or at the anchorage off the port. Bulk carriers and general cargo ships open up their holds and hatch covers for gauging after discharge, and to ballast tanks the crew can make safe; ferries on the Bari service can be gauged between sailings, with vehicle decks and ramps the usual focus. Product tankers at the liquid terminal allow deck and deck piping gauging under the terminal's safety rules. The ship's agent arranges port access, passes and launches.

In the Bay of Kotor, cruise ships can be gauged on call days, mainly for scrubber piping and technical spaces, although work on a ship at anchor depends on tender traffic and the master's agreement. The Bijela refit facility and the Tivat marina area handle large steel-hulled yachts, whose hull plating, tanks and structure can be gauged during refit periods when the yacht is out of the water. For commercial dockings, owners normally use yards elsewhere in the Adriatic, such as Rijeka, and hull gauging in Montenegro beforehand gives the yard a head start on its specification.
list: Port of Bar bulk and general cargo terminals — hold, hatch cover and ballast tank gauging on bulk carriers and general cargo ships once discharged
Bar ferry terminal — ro-pax ferries on the Bari route, gauged on vehicle decks, ramps and ballast tanks in the hours between sailings
Bar liquid cargo terminal — deck and deck piping gauging on product tankers discharging fuel, within the terminal's safety rules
Anchorage off Bar — open-coast anchorage where launch transfers allow sale and charter condition gauging in suitable weather
Kotor cruise berths and inner-bay anchorage — cruise ships calling at the walled town, gauged in technical spaces around tender operations
Bijela and Tivat, Bay of Kotor — gauging of steel plating, tanks and structure on large yachts during refit periods out of the water

context.h: Port state control, EU links and emissions context in Montenegro
p: Montenegro became a full member of the Paris MoU on 1 July 2023, so foreign ships in Bar and Kotor are now inspected under the same regime as ships in Italian and Croatian ports. For owners of older bulk and general cargo ships trading in the region, structural condition at Bar is assessed against the same inspection standards as at Paris MoU ports across the Adriatic, and gauging known corrosion areas before the call is a sensible precaution. The ECA boundary is geographical, so Montenegrin waters have been part of the Mediterranean SOx ECA since 1 May 2025 like those of its EU neighbours: ships off Bar and in the Bay of Kotor need 0.10% sulphur fuel or an equivalent scrubber.

Montenegro is not in the EU, although it is a candidate for membership and uses the euro. Under EU ETS, which has covered shipping since 2024, half of the emissions on a voyage between an EU port and a non-EU port such as Bar fall within the scheme, and FuelEU Maritime, applying since 2025, treats such voyages in a similar way. Owners on the Bari ferry route and on cargo trades with Italy and Croatia therefore feel both regimes, and they weigh steel condition alongside them when deciding how long to keep older tonnage. Montenegro is outside the Schengen area and applies its own visa rules, which affects how a team from India is mobilised.

jobs.h: Typical thickness gauging jobs in Bar and Kotor
jobs.p: Bar jobs are short and practical. Bulk carriers and general cargo ships give a cargo call, ferries give the hours between sailings, and an anchored ship gives as long as the owner chooses. In the Bay of Kotor, cruise call days and yacht refits add a different kind of work. We agree scope, access and reporting with the superintendent before the team travels, and check visa requirements at the same time.
list: Hold frame and hatch cover gauging on a bulk carrier after discharge at Bar, closing out substantial corrosion items ahead of its intermediate survey
Pre-purchase gauging on a general cargo ship at anchor off Bar, giving the buyer a measured view of deck, hold and ballast tank condition
Vehicle deck and ballast tank gauging on a ro-pax ferry on the Bar–Bari route during its turnaround, ahead of a winter docking elsewhere
Scrubber overboard piping survey on a cruise ship berthed at Kotor, timed around passenger operations and tender traffic in the inner bay
Yacht hull thickness gauging of steel plating and tanks on a large yacht in refit at Bijela, before the refit specification is fixed

logistics: Podgorica Airport is the main gateway for Bar, with road and rail links to the coast, and Tivat Airport sits on the Bay of Kotor; Dubrovnik Airport in Croatia is also within reach of the bay. The ship's agent arranges port passes at Bar and Kotor and launches for ships at anchor, and yacht refit facilities issue their own site access. Montenegro is outside the Schengen area and sets its own entry rules, so we confirm current visa requirements for our Indian technicians as soon as an enquiry arrives and build that lead time into the plan.

faqs.q: Do you need a separate visa to work in Montenegro?
faqs.a: Montenegro is outside the Schengen area and applies its own entry rules. When we scope a job we check the current requirements for Indian nationals, including whether an existing Schengen visa is accepted for entry, and build the lead time into the mobilisation plan. Early notice of a Bar or Kotor job therefore helps more than it would for an EU port.

faqs.q: Has Paris MoU membership changed inspections in Bar?
faqs.a: Since Montenegro became a full Paris MoU member, foreign ships in Bar and Kotor are inspected under the same regime as in Italian or Croatian ports. For older ships trading in the region, that makes it sensible to gauge known corrosion areas and close out outstanding survey items before calling, rather than having them raised during an inspection.

faqs.q: Can you gauge large yachts in refit in the Bay of Kotor?
faqs.a: Yes, on steel-hulled yachts during refit, when the hull is out of the water and tanks are opened. Ultrasonic gauging gives plating and structure thicknesses for the refit specification and the yacht's survey. The refit facility issues site access, and we coordinate with its planners so that readings are taken before blasting begins.

faqs.q: Where do ships from Bar go for drydocking?
faqs.a: Usually to a yard in another Adriatic or Mediterranean country, since Bar has no large commercial ship-repair yard. Gauging at Bar beforehand, alongside or at anchor, gives the chosen yard steel estimates for the specification, and the same technicians can then travel to the yard and carry out the docking programme, so the readings stay consistent.
